title: The Nineteen Thirty-Two Bonus Army Eviction
description: An examination of the nineteen thirty-two Bonus Army march in Washington, focusing on veteran encampments, congressional rejection of bonus bills, and the subsequent military eviction ordered by federal authorities.
why_us: Explores a significant historical event using verified archival visual evidence and historical source texts.
timely_basis: A historical documentary adhering to strict archival source constraints.

scenes.narration: During the Great Depression, impoverished World War I veterans traveled to Washington demanding early bonus payments.
Marchers established integrated encampments near the Capitol, living in homemade shacks and lobbying Congress.
Although the House passed a bonus bill in June, the Senate decisively defeated the measure days later.
Legislative rejection left thousands stranded in makeshift camps across the capital as summer conditions deteriorated.
On July twenty-eighth, police attempted to clear abandoned buildings, leading to scuffles and fatal shootings.
Federal troops advanced to clear the remaining demonstrators under orders from military leadership.
Following the eviction, political fallout mounted as the nation reacted to military force used against veterans.
